take_homes: Handing out access and people actually using it are different things, and we count them as one. Ask first what job the colleague is trying to get done.
A rollout needs a people plan as much as a technical one: who owns it, who governs it, who spreads it. If those are unnamed, there is no plan.
Start with one person and one conversation about how they work today. Trust spreads a tool more than a licence does.

monday.move: Have the conversation with one of my HR business partners about how they prepare the weekly people-metrics summary today, and ask what would have to be true for them to use an agent-built draft. I will not put employee data into any tool yet.
monday.stop_condition: If they say they would not trust it or won't use it, I stop and write down why before building anything.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I haven't asked them yet. I'll write to both first.

misconception.why: The story shows decisions and uptake follow trust between people, and agents didn't change that. That makes 'which roles go first' look too simple. I still think headcount will come up in the leadership meeting, and the module never answered it.

one_line: The context notes are filler, but the middle part on why people don't use tools you give them is the first thing here that talks about people, and I'd send a peer leader for that.
